question.worked_solution:
First, we expand the parentheses:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sec}⁡x(\operatorname{cos}⁡x-{cos}^{3}⁡x)=\operatorname{sec}⁡x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡x-\operatorname{sec}⁡x\cdot {cos}^{3}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we use the identity $\operatorname{sec}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}$ to further simplify the expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sec}⁡x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡x-\operatorname{sec}⁡x\cdot {cos}^{3}⁡x & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡x-\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}\cdot {cos}^{3}⁡x \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}-\frac{{cos}^{3}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}-\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}}{\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}}-\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡x\cdot \cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}}{\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}} \\  & =1-{cos}^{2}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can use the identity ${sin}^{2}⁡x=1-{cos}^{2}⁡x$ to rewrite the expression on the right-hand side.

Therefore, we conclude that:

$$
\operatorname{sec}⁡x(\operatorname{cos}⁡x-{cos}^{3}⁡x)={sin}^{2}⁡x
$$
